facts.fact_text: The applicants are members and/or sympathisers of the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP).

On 26 December 2001, the parliamentary group of the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) informed Chişinău Municipal Council of its intention to hold a meeting with its supporters on 9 January 2002.
The meeting intended by the parliamentary group of the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) was to be held in the Square of the Great National Assembly, in front of the Government buildings.
The parliamentary group of the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) stated that the meeting would relate to the introduction of the compulsory study of Russian in schools.
On 9 January 2002, the parliamentary group of the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) held a gathering in the Square of the Great National Assembly, in front of Government headquarters.
The parliamentary group of the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) also held gatherings on 11, 13, 15, 16 and 17 January 2002.

By its decision of 21 February 2002, the Buiucani District Court found the first applicant, Mr Roşca, guilty of having organised and actively participated in the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) demonstrations between 9 and 31 January 2002, in breach of Article 174/1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

By its decision of 21 February 2002, the Buiucani District Court found the second applicant, Mr Secareanu, guilty of having organised and actively participated in the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) demonstrations between 9 and 31 January 2002, in breach of Article 174/1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

By its decision of 24 January 2002, the Buiucani District Court found the third applicant, Mr Buburuz, guilty of having participated in a Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) demonstration on 15 January 2002, in breach of Article 174/1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

By its decision of 29 January 2002, the Buiucani District Court found the fourth applicant, Mr Roşcovan, guilty of having participated in a demonstration on 20 January 2004, in breach of Article 174/1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

By its decision of 24 January 2002, the Buiucani District Court found the fifth applicant, Mr Eremia, guilty of having participated in a demonstration on 13 January 2004, in breach of Article 174/1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

On 14 January 2002, the Ministry of Justice issued an official warning to the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) in accordance with section 27 of the Parties and other Socio-Political Organisations Act.

The Ministry of Justice warned the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) that if it failed to comply with the warning, the Ministry would impose a temporary ban (suspendarea activităţii) on the party's activities in accordance with section 29 of the Parties and other Socio-Political Organisations Act.

On 18 January 2002, the Ministry of Justice issued a decision imposing a one-month ban on the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP)'s activities, in accordance with section 29 of the Parties and other Socio-Political Organisations Act.
On 24 January 2002, the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) challenged the decision of the Ministry of Justice of 18 January 2002.

On 7 March 2002, the Court of Appeal found in favour of the Ministry of Justice and ruled that the decision of 18 January 2002 imposing a one-month ban on the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP)'s activities had been lawful.

On 17 May 2002, a panel of the Supreme Court of Justice delivered its judgment dismissing the appeal lodged by the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) against the Court of Appeal's decision of 7 March 2002.
On unspecified dates, the district police compiled administrative case files in connection with the applicants' participation in unauthorised demonstrations.
The administrative cases against the applicants were referred to the Buiucani District Court.

By its decision of 21 February 2002, the Buiucani District Court found the first applicant, Mr Roşca, guilty of having organised and actively participated in the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) demonstrations between 9 and 31 January 2002, in breach of Article 174/1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

By its decision of 21 February 2002, the Buiucani District Court found the second applicant, Mr Secareanu, guilty of having organised and actively participated in the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) demonstrations between 9 and 31 January 2002, in breach of Article 174/1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

By its decision of 24 January 2002, the Buiucani District Court found the third applicant, Mr Buburuz, guilty of having participated in a Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) demonstration on 15 January 2002, in breach of Article 174/1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

By its decision of 29 January 2002, the Buiucani District Court found the fourth applicant, Mr Roşcovan, guilty of having participated in a demonstration on 20 January 2004, in breach of Article 174/1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

By its decision of 24 January 2002, the Buiucani District Court found the fifth applicant, Mr Eremia, guilty of having participated in a demonstration on 13 January 2004, in breach of Article 174/1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Buiucani District Court imposed an administrative fine of MDL 450 (EUR 40) on the first applicant, Mr Roşca.
The Buiucani District Court imposed an administrative fine of MDL 450 (EUR 40) on the second applicant, Mr Secareanu.
The Buiucani District Court imposed an administrative fine of MDL 90 (EUR 8) on the third applicant, Mr Buburuz.
The Buiucani District Court imposed an administrative fine of MDL 90 (EUR 8) on the fourth applicant, Mr Roşcovan.
The Buiucani District Court imposed an administrative fine of MDL 90 (EUR 8) on the fifth applicant, Mr Eremia.
By its decision of 30 April 2002, the Chişinău Regional Court dismissed the appeal of the first applicant, Mr Roşca, against the Buiucani District Court judgment.
By its decision of 30 April 2002, the Chişinău Regional Court dismissed the appeal of the second applicant, Mr Secareanu, against the Buiucani District Court judgment.
By its decision of 13 February 2002, the Chişinău Regional Court dismissed the appeal of the third applicant, Mr Buburuz, against the Buiucani District Court judgment.
By its decision of 28 February 2002, the Chişinău Regional Court dismissed the appeal of the fourth applicant, Mr Roşcovan, against the Buiucani District Court judgment.
By its decision of 13 February 2002, the Chişinău Regional Court dismissed the appeal of the fifth applicant, Mr Eremia, against the Buiucani District Court judgment.

The parliamentary group of the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) relied on section 22 of the Status of Members of Parliament Act, which according to the CDPP did not require members of Parliament to obtain prior authorisation for meetings with their supporters.

By a decision of 3 January 2002, Chişinău Municipal Council classified the gathering to be held on 9 January 2002 as a 'demonstration' within the meaning of sections 4, 8, 12 and 13 of the Assemblies Act.

On 23 January 2002, Chişinău Municipal Council addressed a letter to the Ministry of Justice informing it that there was a discrepancy between the provisions of the Status of Members of Parliament Act and those of the Assemblies Act.
Chişinău Municipal Council informed the Ministry of Justice that it did not know which of the Status of Members of Parliament Act or the Assemblies Act to apply.

Chişinău Municipal Council stated that a number of reputable lawyers supported the idea that the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) members of Parliament had the right to hold meetings with their supporters in the Square of the Great National Assembly without obtaining prior authorisation, in accordance with sections 22 and 23 of the Status of Members of Parliament Act.

Chişinău Municipal Council requested the Ministry of Justice to ask Parliament for an official interpretation of the legislation in question regarding the discrepancy between the Status of Members of Parliament Act and the Assemblies Act.

On 26 January 2002, Chişinău Municipal Council issued a decision noting that the provisions of domestic legislation were contradictory in respect of the demonstrations organised by the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) and that the opinions of legal experts were contradictory.

In its decision of 26 January 2002, Chişinău Municipal Council stated that it had formally requested the Ministry of Justice to ask Parliament for an official and urgent interpretation of the relevant legislation.
In its decision of 26 January 2002, Chişinău Municipal Council suspended its decision of 3 January 2002 until Parliament had given its official interpretation of the relevant legislation.

The Ministry of Justice claimed that the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP)'s gatherings were not meetings with voters within the meaning of the Status of Members of Parliament Act, but demonstrations falling under the Assemblies Act.

The President of the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) relied on section 22 of the Status of Members of Parliament Act, arguing that it was a very specific act applicable to meetings between members of Parliament and voters, while the Assemblies Act was general in nature.

The Ministry of Justice stated that the gatherings organised by the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) on 9, 10, 11, 13, 15, 16 and 17 January 2002 had in fact been demonstrations and marches and therefore fell within the scope of the Assemblies Act rather than the Status of Members of Parliament Act.

According to the Ministry of Justice's decision of 18 January 2002, the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) had breached the provisions of sections 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 11 of the Assemblies Act by not obtaining prior authorisation from Chişinău Municipal Council to stage demonstrations.
The Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP)'s actions disclosed a violation of sections 27 and 29 of the Parties and other Socio-Political Organisations Act.
The Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP)'s actions disclosed a violation of section 15(1) and (2) of the Status of Members of Parliament Act.

The Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) argued in its challenge that the gatherings had been meetings with voters within the meaning of the Status of Members of Parliament Act, and not assemblies falling within the scope of the Assemblies Act.

The Court of Appeal found that the gatherings organised by the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) had in fact been demonstrations, meetings and marches which fell under the provisions of the Assemblies Act, and not meetings with voters.

The Court of Appeal found that even assuming the gatherings had been intended as meetings with voters, they had gradually taken on the nature of demonstrations and accordingly the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) needed authorisation in order to organise them.
The Ministry of Justice did not reply to Chişinău Municipal Council's request of 23 January 2002 for interpretation of the law.
The Ministry of Justice did not address any request to Parliament regarding the interpretation of the law following Chişinău Municipal Council's request of 23 January 2002.

The Supreme Court of Justice stated in its ruling of 25 February 2002 that even if the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) had the initial intention of holding meetings with its supporters, those meetings later took on the character of demonstrations, marches, processions and picketing, which fall under the provisions of the Organisation and Conduct of Assemblies Act.

The Supreme Court of Justice stated in its ruling of 25 February 2002 that the leaders of the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) were required to comply with the provisions of the Assemblies Act.
The relevant domestic law applicable to this case was set out in Christian Democratic People's Party v. Moldova, no. 28793/02, §§ 34-41, ECHR 2006-.

According to the Ministry of Justice's decision of 18 January 2002, the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) had breached the provisions of sections 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 11 of the Assemblies Act by blocking public roads.
The participation of minors in the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) demonstrations had been in breach of Article 15 of the International Convention on the Rights of the Child.
The participation of minors in the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) demonstrations had been in breach of section 13(3) of the Protection of Children Act.
The participation of minors in the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) demonstrations had been in breach of section 56(g) of the Education Act.

The use of the slogan 'I'd rather be dead than a Communist' (mai bine mort decât comunist) at the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) demonstrations could be interpreted as a call to public violence and an act undermining the legal and constitutional order.

The Court of Appeal stated that as a result of the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) demonstrations, the public transport company had suffered losses of 12,133 Moldovan lei (MDL) (approximately 1,050 euros (EUR) at the time).

The Court of Appeal stated that the participation of minors in the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) demonstrations had been in breach of the International Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Protection of Children Act and the Education Act.
Towards the end of 2001, the Government of Moldova made public its intention to make the study of the Russian language compulsory in schools for children aged seven and over.
The Government of Moldova's initiative to make the study of the Russian language compulsory in schools prompted vehement criticism from the opposition.
The Government of Moldova's initiative to make the study of the Russian language compulsory in schools generated a heated public debate.
The parliamentary group of the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) stated that the meeting would relate to the introduction of the compulsory study of Russian in schools.
Chişinău Municipal Council did not give any reasons for the change of location from the Square of the Great National Assembly to the Square of the National Opera.

The Ministry of Justice warned the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) that if it failed to comply with the warning, the Ministry would impose a temporary ban (suspendarea activităţii) on the party's activities in accordance with section 29 of the Parties and other Socio-Political Organisations Act.

On 18 January 2002, the Ministry of Justice issued a decision imposing a one-month ban on the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP)'s activities, in accordance with section 29 of the Parties and other Socio-Political Organisations Act.
On 8 February 2002, the Ministry of Justice issued a decision lifting the temporary ban imposed on the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP)'s activities.

The Ministry of Justice lifted the temporary ban on the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP)'s activities following an inquiry made by the Secretary General of the Council of Europe under Article 52 of the Convention.
The decision of the Ministry of Justice of 8 February 2002 did not set aside the decision of 18 January 2002 imposing the temporary ban on the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP)'s activities.

The Supreme Court of Justice endorsed the arguments of the Court of Appeal and found that since the demonstrations organised by the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) had been illegal, the sanction imposed on it had not been disproportionate.

The Supreme Court of Justice stated that in any event the decision of the Ministry of Justice of 18 January 2002 had not had any negative effects on the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) since it had not been enforced, the CDPP's accounts had not been frozen and the party could continue its activities unhindered.
The Buiucani District Court imposed an administrative fine of MDL 450 (EUR 40) on the first applicant, Mr Roşca.
The Buiucani District Court imposed an administrative fine of MDL 450 (EUR 40) on the second applicant, Mr Secareanu.
The Buiucani District Court imposed an administrative fine of MDL 90 (EUR 8) on the third applicant, Mr Buburuz.
The Buiucani District Court imposed an administrative fine of MDL 90 (EUR 8) on the fourth applicant, Mr Roşcovan.
The Buiucani District Court imposed an administrative fine of MDL 90 (EUR 8) on the fifth applicant, Mr Eremia.
The Chişinău Regional Court gave no reasons for dismissing the applicants' appeals against the Buiucani District Court judgments.
